findings.description: inputBoxHolds is the strict 'paste landed whole' predicate, so tellConductor's !inputBoxHolds treats any box it can't match as landed: no input box parsed, a partial paste missing its head, or a leftover draft in front of the message. It then skips the second Enter.

The tell pastes into the conductor's input box without checking that it is empty first. Text already there (the operator's draft, or a message an earlier failed tell left behind) gets submitted joined to the new message with no separator, and the CLI still prints that the message landed.

`load-buffer -` and `paste-buffer -d` use unnamed buffers, so the paste takes whatever buffer is on top of the server's stack. Two writers on the conductor socket can swap or mix their texts: the tell plus the watchdog's `steerPane(conductor, CONDUCTOR_NUDGE)`, or operator copy-mode while attached via `pup attach`. The tell's buffer is then left on the server. Naming both ends (`-b pup-<pid>-<n>`) closes it.

The pasteText JSDoc and decision 85 (docs/09-decisions.md L4410-4411) say the tell text stays off any command line because an argv is readable by every process on the machine. But `pup conductor tell <message>` (src/cli/index.ts L979, L996) puts the same text on pup's own argv (/proc/<pid>/cmdline) for the whole tell: the paste settle plus up to two submit beats. So the stated control does not hold end to end. Either say the text is off tmux's argv only (pup's own argv has it, as `pup steer` already does), or read the message from stdin.

attachConductor is the only tmux call in the runtime that skips `env: tmuxEnv()`. Decision 47 says every tmux call drops $TMUX, PUP_*, ^CLAUDE, ^ANTHROPIC_ and NODE_OPTIONS. If the conductor's server is gone between the isConductorRunning check and the spawn, `tmux -L pup-conductor-<id> attach` can start a server on that computable socket. That server's global environment (`show-environment -g`) would hold the operator's unscrubbed environment. This is narrow: it needs that race, and the server only stays up if the operator's tmux.conf creates a session. Passing `env: tmuxEnv()` closes it and keeps TERM, PATH and TMUX_TMPDIR. The medium confidence rests on attach-session being able to start a server, which is tmux behaviour I did not read in its source.

The diff adds the refusal `'No conductor is running for this project; start one with \`pup conductor start\`.'` twice, once in the CLI `attach` action and once in core `tellConductor`. If the wording changes in one place, the other drifts. Exporting it from `conductor.service.ts`, which already owns `isConductorRunning`, gives both commands one copy.

`tellOrRefuse` catches with `isRefusedSteer`, which also lets `SteerNotDeliveredError` through. The tell path can't throw that error. `pasteIntoPane`, `submitPane` and `inputBoxHolds` go through `tmuxAt`, whose only typed error is `SessionPaneMissingError`. So the catch suggests a "steer not delivered" outcome the tell never produces. `error instanceof SessionPaneMissingError` would state the real contract.

An unknown conductor verb with a message, such as `pup conductor foo hi`, now gets "`pup conductor foo` takes no message" instead of the "Unknown conductor action" error. That points the operator at the wrong problem. Move the `message !== undefined` check below the unknown-verb check, or restrict it to `start` and `stop`.

In decision 85, "The text rides tmux's stdin through `load-buffer -` and `paste-buffer -p` names only the pane" fuses two clauses, so it reads as if the text rides through `paste-buffer -p`. Add a comma: "…through `load-buffer -`, and `paste-buffer -p` names only the pane, so…".

In the tellConductor JSDoc, "Pasted through a tmux buffer, never typed by `send-keys`, so the text is on no command line." repeats what the pasteText JSDoc in session-runtime.service.ts already says, and nothing in it is specific to the tell. Delete the sentence and keep the WHY about the Enter retry.

The `attach` action comment's "the conductor is the pane, and tmux's detach is the way out that keeps it" is cryptic, and the printed hint and decision 85 already say why Ctrl-c and /exit kill the conductor. It could shrink to "Said before the terminal is handed over, since attach blocks until detach."
